posts.why: The legal problem makes the point undeniable.

tiktok.hook: This landing page promises six impossible things. One of them is a legal problem.
beats: One hundred customers in a week
tiktok.vo: This landing page promises six impossible things: guaranteed ranking, one hundred customers in a week, passive income, a business that runs itself, and something about a health outcome that I am not going to repeat on camera because it is the one that could get somebody sued. The other five are just expensive, and they work about as well as you would expect, which is not at all and then a refund.
tiktok.cap: Six promises. Five will cost you money. One could cost you more than money.
tiktok.body: Guaranteed ranking, a hundred customers in a week, passive income, a business that runs itself, and one claim I will not repeat on camera. Five are expensive promises and one is a legal problem.

instagram.cap:
The list is always the same shape. The more impossible the promise, the higher the price, and the more likely the refund page is a form that nobody answers.

If the promise is impossible, the price is not the expensive part.

facebook.body:
A landing page I read promises six impossible things: guaranteed ranking, a hundred customers in a week, passive income, a business that runs itself, and one claim I will not repeat on camera because it is a legal problem.

The other five are just expensive, and they work about as well as you would expect — not at all, then a refund.

Which promise would make you close the page?

posts.topic: The sentence that loses the sale
posts.why: Names the exact phrase that triggers suspicion.

tiktok.hook: A promise of results is the sentence that loses the sale.
tiktok.vo: A promise of results is the sentence that loses the sale, because nobody believes it and everybody notices it. The moment you promise an outcome you do not control, the reader starts looking for the other places you might be stretching, and they find them, because everybody stretches somewhere. Say the limit instead and the reader relaxes, because you have just proved you are not doing that.
tiktok.cap: One unbelievable promise makes every true sentence suspect.
tiktok.body: Nobody believes a promise of results and everybody notices it. The reader starts looking for the other places you might be stretching, and they find them — every business stretches somewhere.

instagram.cap:
A limit costs you the buyers who wanted a guarantee and wins the ones who wanted a professional. On balance, that is a good trade.

Trust is spent in one direction and rebuilt slowly.

facebook.body:
A promise of results is usually the sentence that loses the sale.

Nobody believes it. Everybody notices it. And the moment you promise an outcome you do not control, the reader starts hunting for the other places you might be stretching.

Say the limit instead. The reader relaxes, because you have just proved you are not doing that.

What is your limit?

posts.why: Gives exact words to copy, which is what makes a teach post work.

tiktok.hook: Write your own limit into the sales copy. Here are three that work.
beats: This will not bring you customers
Nobody will do it for you
tiktok.vo: Write your own limit into the sales copy, in the same paragraph as the price. Three that work: this will not bring you customers. This is not a course and there is no call. Nobody will do any of it for you. Every one of those sentences loses a few buyers and wins the ones who were going to be difficult, which is the same buyer, described twice.
tiktok.cap: "This will not bring you customers." Try writing it above your price.
tiktok.body: One limit, in the same paragraph as the price. This will not bring you customers. This is not a course and there is no call. Nobody will do it for you. Each loses a few buyers and wins the ones who would have complained.

instagram.cap:
A limit functions as a filter and a proof at the same time, which is why it is the cheapest trust-building sentence available to a small business.

The buyers you lose to a limit were going to be difficult anyway.

facebook.body:
Write your own limit into the sales copy, in the same paragraph as the price.

Three that work:
— This will not bring you customers.
— This is not a course and there is no call.
— Nobody will do any of it for you.

Each one loses a few buyers and wins the ones who would otherwise have been difficult.

Which is the same buyer, described twice.

posts.why: A competitive claim with no invented numbers.

tiktok.hook: Honesty is the only unfair advantage left in Nigerian marketing.
beats: It is free and it is rare
tiktok.vo: Honesty is the only unfair advantage left in Nigerian marketing, and I mean that practically. Everyone is shouting, everyone has a guarantee, everyone is the leading provider. Almost nobody says what their product does not do or who should not buy it. One honest sentence stands out more than a bigger budget, and it costs nothing to write.
tiktok.cap: Everyone is shouting. Almost nobody is admitting. Admit something.
tiktok.body: Everyone has a guarantee and everyone is the leading provider. Almost nobody says what their product will not do. One honest sentence stands out more than a bigger budget, and it costs nothing.

instagram.cap:
It is rare because it feels like weakness. It reads as confidence, which is why the businesses that do it are remembered.

A limit is the cheapest competitive advantage in the market.

facebook.body:
Honesty is the only unfair advantage left in Nigerian marketing, and I mean that practically.

Everyone is shouting. Everyone has a guarantee. Everyone is the leading provider.

Almost nobody says what their product does not do, or who should not buy it.

One honest sentence stands out more than a bigger budget, and it costs nothing to write.

What could you admit?

posts.topic: The limit is why he paid
posts.why: A buyer's own words are the strongest proof.

tiktok.hook: A buyer said the line about what it will not do is why he paid.
beats: He had been lied to before
So he looked for the limit
tiktok.vo: A buyer told me the line that made him pay was the one saying the pack would not bring him customers. He said he had bought two things before that promised him customers and neither worked, so when he saw a seller admit the limit he assumed the rest of the page was also true. He bought the bundle. The sentence I was most nervous about is the one that closed it.
tiktok.cap: "The line saying it wouldn't bring me customers is why I paid."
tiktok.body: He had bought two things that promised customers and neither worked. Seeing a seller admit the limit made him assume the rest of the page was true, so he bought the bundle.

instagram.cap:
People who have been burned are not looking for bigger promises. They are looking for evidence that this seller knows where their product stops.

The sentence you are most nervous about is usually the one that closes.

facebook.body:
A buyer told me the line that made him pay was the one saying the pack would not bring him customers.

He had bought two things before that promised him customers. Neither worked.

So when he saw a seller admit the limit, he assumed the rest of the page was true too. He bought the bundle.

The sentence I was most nervous about is the one that closed it.

posts.topic: Name the limit next to the price

tiktok.hook: Put the limit in the same paragraph as the price. Not on a separate page nobody reads.
tiktok.vo: Put the limit in the same paragraph as the price, not hidden on an FAQ page nine screens down. Same paragraph, same breath: it is five thousand naira, and it will not bring you customers. The proximity is the whole trick, because a limit next to a price reads as honesty and a limit in the terms reads as a legal department.
tiktok.cap: Same paragraph as the price. Proximity is what makes it read as honesty.
tiktok.body: A limit next to a price reads as honesty. The same limit in the terms reads as a legal department. Put it in the same breath as the number.

instagram.cap:
Placement changes meaning. This is true of prices, guarantees, and anything you were tempted to bury.

A disclaimer at the bottom is a warning. A limit at the price is a promise.

facebook.body:
Put the limit in the same paragraph as the price.

Not on an FAQ page nine screens down. Same paragraph, same breath: 'It is ₦5,000, and it will not bring you customers.'

The proximity is the whole trick. A limit next to a price reads as honesty. The same limit in the terms reads as a legal department.

Where is yours?

posts.why: A short economic argument that is hard to argue with.

tiktok.hook: Every promise you cannot keep is a refund and a review.
beats: The sale is not the end
It is the start of the obligation
tiktok.vo: Every promise you cannot keep is a refund and a review, and the review is worse than the refund. The sale is not the end of the transaction, it is the beginning of an obligation you have to meet every day for as long as the business exists. Which is why the safest promise is a small one you can keep on a Tuesday when everything is going wrong.
tiktok.cap: The refund is a cost. The review is a sentence that outlives you.
tiktok.body: The sale is the start of an obligation, not the end of a transaction. The safest promise is a small one you can keep on a Tuesday when everything is going wrong.

instagram.cap:
Most overpromising happens on a good day, which is exactly why it fails on a bad one. Write the promise on a bad day.

Promise what you can do on your worst day, not your best.

facebook.body:
Every promise you cannot keep is a refund and a review — and the review is worse than the refund.

The sale is not the end of the transaction. It is the beginning of an obligation you have to meet every day for as long as the business exists.

Which is why the safest promise is a small one you can keep on a Tuesday when everything is going wrong.

What is your promise?

posts.topic: What makes you distrust an ad
posts.why: The audience names the exact word we avoid.

tiktok.hook: I asked what makes people distrust an ad. One word came up over and over.
beats: It means you are about to lie
tiktok.vo: I asked what makes people distrust an ad. Almost everyone said the same word: guarantee. And when I asked why, they said because nobody can guarantee that, so they are either lying or they do not understand their own product. One man said if you have to promise it in capitals, it is probably not true, which is the whole argument of this video and he did it in a sentence.
tiktok.cap: "If you have to promise it in capitals, it is probably not true."
tiktok.body: Almost everyone said the same word: guarantee. Because nobody can guarantee that, so either they are lying or they do not understand their own product.

instagram.cap:
This is why we write limits instead. It is not modesty, it is a response to how people actually read advertising.

The word meant to reassure is the word that raises suspicion.

facebook.body:
I asked what makes people distrust an ad.

Almost everyone said the same word: 'guarantee'.

And when I asked why, they said because nobody can guarantee that — so either the seller is lying or they do not understand their own product.

One man put it better: 'If you have to promise it in capitals, it is probably not true.'

Which word makes you close a page?

posts.topic: It will not get you one customer
posts.why: The clearest possible statement of what ₦5,000 does.

tiktok.hook: The bundle will not get you one single customer. Here is what it does instead.
beats: For the ones already in your inbox
tiktok.vo: The bundle will not get you one single customer. It does not do advertising, it does not bring traffic, and it will not make anybody message you. What it does is give you the words for the people who already messaged and went quiet, which in most small businesses is the largest untapped thing they own. If you need traffic, that is a different job and I will tell you honestly that this is the wrong purchase.
tiktok.cap: No customers. Scripts for the ones you have. ₦35,000 all nine, ₦5,000 each. WhatsApp 0905 069 0837.
tiktok.body: No traffic, no ads, no new messages. It gives you the words for people who already messaged and went quiet, which is usually the largest untapped thing a small business owns.

instagram.cap:
If your inbox is empty, this is the wrong purchase. If your inbox has people who went quiet, it is exactly the right one.

The honest version of a marketing product: it does not market for you.

facebook.body:
The bundle will not get you one single customer.

It does not do advertising. It does not bring traffic. It will not make anybody message you.

What it does is give you the words for the people who already messaged and went quiet — which in most small businesses is the largest untapped thing they own.

If you need traffic, this is the wrong purchase and I will say so.

₦5,000 each, ₦35,000 for all nine.

posts.why: The alternative wording is the lesson.

tiktok.hook: A client wanted results guaranteed in the ad. We wrote we cannot guarantee results instead.
tiktok.vo: A client wanted the words results guaranteed across the top of his advert. We wrote we cannot guarantee results, but here is exactly what we do and how long it takes, instead. He was nervous for a week. The honest version converted better, and more importantly, nobody came back angry, which is the cost that does not show up in a dashboard. A guarantee is not confidence. It is a liability with good posture.
tiktok.cap: A guarantee is not confidence. It is a liability with good posture.
tiktok.body: He wanted results guaranteed across the top. We wrote we cannot guarantee results, here is exactly what we do and how long it takes. It converted better and nobody came back angry.

slides: Asked for: a guarantee of results
instagram.cap:
Specificity is what actually reassures people. How long it takes, what exactly happens, what it costs — those three beat any guarantee.

The cost that does not show on a dashboard is the angry customer.

facebook.body:
A client wanted 'results guaranteed' across the top of his advert.

We wrote 'we cannot guarantee results, but here is exactly what we do and how long it takes' instead.

He was nervous for a week. The honest version converted better — and nobody came back angry, which is the cost that never shows up on a dashboard.

A guarantee is not confidence. It is a liability with good posture.

posts.why: A one-evening exercise with a visible outcome.

tiktok.hook: Read your last advert and delete every promise you cannot prove. Then see if it still works.
tiktok.vo: Read your last advert and delete every promise you cannot prove. Strike them out, all of them, and read what is left. If the advert still says something, that is your offer and you should lead with it. If it says nothing, then the promises were the whole advert, and that is worth knowing before a customer finds out for you.
tiktok.cap: Strike out every unprovable promise. What is left is your actual offer.
tiktok.body: Strike out every promise you cannot prove and read what is left. If it still says something, that is your offer. If it says nothing, the promises were the entire advert.

instagram.cap:
This is uncomfortable the first time and clarifying every time after. Most adverts lose about half their words and all of their noise.

An advert with the promises removed is a useful mirror.

facebook.body:
Read your last advert and delete every promise you cannot prove.

Strike them all out. Read what is left.

If it still says something, that is your offer, and you should be leading with it.

If it says nothing, the promises were the entire advert — which is worth knowing before a customer finds out for you.

Try it tonight.
